items.summary: ISC2 is recruiting 3,000 volunteers for a pilot exam phase of its forthcoming AI security certification, expected to launch in early 2027.

items.title: DreamHost incident triggers password resets, locks customers out of email and FTP accounts
items.summary: DreamHost restored its File Manager after an incident that disrupted services, but customers still cannot access email or FTP accounts until passwords are reset.

items.title: This is Fine: What NetScaler Zero-Days Tell Us About the New Normal
items.summary: An article highlights the need for continuous patch management for Citrix NetScaler, noting that recent zero‑days illustrate a new normal for security operations.

items.title: From federal SOCs to Talos: Ryan Fetterman on practical security research
items.summary: Security researcher Ryan Fetterman discusses detection engineering and building a blue‑team career without burnout, emphasizing practical approaches to security research.

items.title: What happens when security tools go dark before the ransomware
items.summary:
A China-linked ransomware group disabled security tools at a critical infrastructure operator before launching an encryptor.
The incident shows many security budgets do not account for pre-attack tool shutdowns.

items.title: Dead Popcorn Time Updater Put Millions of Computers at Risk of Takeover
items.summary:
A malicious Popcorn Time updater ran at system boot, repeatedly polling its update domain to execute privileged code.
Millions of computers were exposed to potential takeover.

items.title: Watchdog Urges Police and Fire Service to Improve Cybersecurity
items.summary:
UK police forces and fire and rescue services have been urged to strengthen cybersecurity.
The call comes as cyber threats outpace current defenses.

items.title: Australia Gets Into Amadey Malware Backend, Cuts Off Access to 180,000 Infected Computers
items.summary:
Australia's ASD accessed the Amadey malware backend and disabled the criminal's control over 180,000 infected computers worldwide.
The move cut off data theft and remote access.

items.title: Energy giant ENGIE discloses data breach affecting customers
items.summary:
ENGIE disclosed a data breach that exposed customer information after attackers compromised a marketing platform used by its business partners.
The breach involved customer data theft.

items.title: OpenAI Compaction Flaw Let Researchers Bypass Hidden Reasoning Protections
items.summary:
Security researchers showed that OpenAI's compaction feature can bypass encrypted hidden reasoning, exposing internal model logic.
The flaw allows copying of hidden reasoning in plain text.

items.title: CISA confirms PHP2Shell vulnerabilities now exploited in attacks
items.summary:
CISA confirmed that PHP2Shell vulnerabilities are actively exploited and directed federal agencies to patch systems by Thursday.
The vulnerabilities are now in its catalog of exploited flaws.

items.title: Maritime Coalition Launches Free Vulnerability Database for Ship and Port Systems
items.summary:
A maritime coalition released a free vulnerability database cataloguing nearly 30,000 IT and OT weaknesses, including 37 maritime-specific products.
The database is intended for ships and port systems.

items.title: Attackers Hijack Dahua IP Cameras in Ukraine Using P2P Access and Auth Weaknesses
items.summary:
Ukraine's CERT warned that attackers exploited P2P access and authentication weaknesses to hijack Dahua IP cameras.
The breach allowed remote viewing, configuration changes, and creation of third‑party accounts.

items.title: Several AI security market categories are headed for bigger platforms
items.summary:
An analyst predicts that many AI security startups will be absorbed into larger platforms, with funding concentrating on fewer, bigger players.
The trend reflects a shift toward integrated security solutions.

items.title: Microsoft Authenticator vulnerability let rogue Android apps steal work account access
items.summary: Researchers discovered a flaw in Microsoft Authenticator on Android that allowed rogue apps to silently take over work accounts without permissions or user interaction. Updating the app is required to mitigate the risk.

items.title: LLM agent security needs more than guardrails
items.summary: Concentric AI’s Chief Scientist explains that securing LLM agents depends more on controlling input data than on model guardrails. Guardrails reduce but cannot eliminate bad outcomes; data controls are essential.

items.title: Amutable Foundations is a Linux system with no SSH and no package manager
items.summary: Amutable Foundations is a Linux distribution that eliminates SSH and package managers, instead sending signed reports of software and configuration. Engineers maintain code in the kernel, systemd, and image‑building tools.

items.title: 71% of vulnerability exploitation starts within a week of disclosure
items.summary: Rapid7 reports that 71% of high‑severity vulnerability exploitation occurs within a week of public disclosure, with an average of three days between disclosure and attack.

items.title: Cybersecurity jobs available right now: October 27, 2026
items.summary: A listing for a Cybersecurity Expert / Penetration Tester in Sweden is no longer accepting applications. The role involves testing web applications, APIs, and evaluating AI‑driven security testing.

items.title: CISA Confirms Active Exploitation of Two PHP2Shell Flaws Enabling Remote Code Execution
items.summary: CISA added two PHP2Shell vulnerabilities (CVE‑2026‑109618 and CVE‑2026‑109619) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after confirming active exploitation that enables unauthenticated remote code execution.

items.title: GPT-6.1 Terra meets OpenAI’s Critical cyber threshold, and it’s cheaper than GPT-5.6 Terra
items.summary: OpenAI released GPT‑6.1 Terra, a desktop‑software‑operating model, with API pricing 50% lower than GPT‑5.6 Terra. Prices are $1 per million input tokens, $0.05 per million cached input tokens, and $5 per million output tokens.

items.title: Cybersecurity Issue Forces a Major New Mexico Hospital to Divert Patients and Close Clinics
items.summary: The University of New Mexico Health System canceled appointments at over 30 clinics and advised patients not to visit its main hospital due to a cybersecurity incident that forced operational disruptions.

items.title: Japanese virtual desktop cloud hacked so hard it asks to be banned
items.summary: A Japanese virtual desktop cloud service used for foreign exchange trading suffered a severe hack, with the CEO admitting the service had security holes that were slow to fix, leading to calls for banning the platform.

items.title: So Many AI Security Benchmarks, But None Tell the Whole Story
items.summary: A review of AI security benchmarks highlights that many exist, but none fully capture real‑world security, underscoring the need to test models against specific code and workflows.

items.title: Experts temper emergency-level alarms over critical Brotli defect
items.summary: Open‑source Brotli library defect triggered an emergency response. No wild exploitation has been observed. Experts advise caution but no immediate threat.

items.title: Worm armed 42 GitHub repos by hiding a payload too big to fail
items.summary: A worm infected 42 GitHub repositories by embedding large payloads (12.9–13.7 MB). Payload size prevented detection by GitHub code search.

items.title: University of Copenhagen data breach exposes data of 525,000 people
items.summary: Hackers accessed a test environment at the University of Copenhagen that contained personal data of 525,000 individuals. The breach involved no known exploitation of the data beyond unauthorized access.

items.title: Risks & Rewards: How AI Is Redefining the CISO's Role
items.summary: Nvidia security executive Mark Weatherford said CISOs must help business leaders weigh AI's benefits and risks. He emphasized that those deploying AI should own the associated risks.

items.title: Alibaba's Qwen AI caught trying to contact server in China
items.summary: Alibaba's Qwen AI model attempted to contact a server in China, likely due to unsanitized training data. No evidence suggests malicious intent beyond this behavior.

items.title: Former pentester used ARTEX AI to steal 8.2 million data records
items.summary: South Korean police identified seven suspects who used the ARTEX AI pentesting framework to breach more than 90 organizations. The attacks resulted in the theft of 8.2 million data records.

items.title: Texas sues OpenAI for deceiving consumers about safety, seeks sweeping reforms and fines
items.summary: Texas filed a lawsuit against OpenAI alleging deceptive trade practices regarding the safety of its AI services. The suit seeks to hold CEO Sam Altman personally liable and pursue sweeping reforms and fines.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: In-the-Wild Attack Abuses AI Agents' Trust in Markdown
items.summary: A new prompt injection technique exploits AI coding assistants' trust in local Markdown instruction files. The attack turns text documents into executable actions, blurring the line between documentation and code.

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.1 Terra with 3x faster AI agents, 50% lower pricing
items.summary: OpenAI launched GPT-6.1 Terra, a model focused on computer use, visual reasoning, coding, and everyday work. The new model offers agents that are three times faster and priced 50% lower than larger models.

items.title: LiteLLM supply chain attack started with an exposed master key
items.summary: A supply chain attack on LiteLLM began with an exposed master key that was not rotated. The incident illustrates the risks of failing to rotate potentially exposed keys.

items.title: Anthropic Files for Potentially the Biggest IPO Ever as CEO Warns of Risk to Humanity From AI
items.summary: Anthropic filed for a large IPO while its CEO warned that rogue AI agents could pose existential risks. Recent hacking incidents involving AI agents have heightened concerns about technology slipping beyond human control.

items.title: DreamHost forces password resets in ongoing "incident"
items.summary: DreamHost forced password resets for email and FTP/SFTP users after an incident disrupted connections to its File Manager interface. The reset was part of the company's response to the ongoing incident.

items.title: Hackers Infect 953 Online Stores With Scanner-Evading JavaScript, Mostly on Magento
items.summary: Unknown threat actor infected 953 online stores, mainly Magento, adding hidden JavaScript via CMS blocks. The code loads malicious scripts when users visit. Campaign active since July 2025.

items.title: Senators, rights groups say Trump administration breaking law by withholding surveillance court opinion
items.summary: Senators and civil‑rights groups claim the Trump administration violated law by withholding the classified opinion on Section 702 of FISA. The decision on the law’s future is pending. The opinion could influence the next FISA renewal.

items.title: 'Gheist' Weaponizes GitHub Tokens to Steal Cloud Secrets
items.summary: The 'Gheist' supply‑chain attack harvests GitHub tokens and sensitive data from thousands of developer repositories. Attackers use stolen credentials to access cloud resources. The campaign continues to expand.

items.title: Microsoft releases emergency .NET security fixes for Google Brotli bug
items.summary: Microsoft issued emergency patches for .NET to address a Brotli compression flaw also affecting Google. The update mitigates potential code execution vulnerabilities. The fix is part of a broader industry response.

items.title: PHP Issues Second Windows Security Update in Five Days to Fix Brotli Code Execution Flaw
items.summary: PHP released updated Windows packages for PHP 8.2‑8.5 to fix CVE‑2026‑111497 in the Brotli library. The flaw allows memory corruption and possible code execution via the cURL extension. Users should update immediately.

items.title: Authorities extradite Chinese national for alleged $37M investment scam
items.summary: Zheng Zhao was extradited for orchestrating a $37 million investment scam that targeted 174 U.S. residents. The scheme involved a fake investment operation linked to Cambodia. Authorities are pursuing charges.

items.title: CVE-2026-111497: Critical out-of-bounds write in the Node.js Brotli decoder
items.summary: Node.js disclosed CVE‑2026‑111497, an out‑of‑bounds write in its Brotli decoder affecting 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x releases. The vulnerability is rated high by Node.js and critical by Google. Attackers can supply crafted Brotli data to exploit it.

items.title: Serbian autocrat loses election following widespread reports of digital repression
items.summary: Serbian leader Aleksandar Vučić conceded defeat in the prime‑minister race after widespread digital repression incidents. The loss followed opposition mobilization. The election outcome signals a shift in Serbian politics.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Ukraine disputes Musk's claims of Starlink misuse as military connectivity restored
items.summary: Ukrainian Defense Minister Yevhen Khmara denied Elon Musk’s allegations that Starlink was misused. He reported that Starlink and Starshield connectivity had been restored for Ukrainian forces. The claim reflects ongoing cyber‑security concerns.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Dutch police extradite Chinese national accused of laundering Cambodian investment scam funds
items.summary: Dutch authorities extradited Zheng Zhao, a 44‑year‑old Chinese national, for laundering funds from a Cambodian‑linked investment scam. Zhao allegedly facilitated money transfers to U.S. victims. The extradition follows a coordinated investigation.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Critical 'HTTP2Shell' Brotli vulnerability triggers emergency patches
items.summary: Critical HTTP2Shell flaw in the Brotli C decoder used by Node.js can corrupt memory and expose sensitive data. Emergency patches have been released by Node.js and Microsoft.

items.title: UK pentester 'killa' claims $2K Bitcoin prize in PHP2Shell capture-the-flag contest
items.summary: UK pentester Jaydip Modhwadia won a $2,000 Bitcoin prize by solving the PHP2Shell capture‑the‑flag challenge in about three hours.

items.title: CISA 2030 Sets Out ‘Aggressive, Anticipatory’ Cyber Defense Strategy for Critical Infrastructure
items.summary: CISA’s 2030 strategy focuses on rapid detection, response, and resilience for critical infrastructure, moving beyond passive defense.

items.title: Attackers Use Microsoft Teams IT Support Scams to Deploy Malware and Ransomware
items.summary: Threat actors use Microsoft Teams’ external chat feature to impersonate IT support, delivering malware and ransomware in hundreds of incidents.

items.title: Trumpets blare and skies part as AI hypefest culminates in Anthropic IPO filing
items.summary: Anthropic filed for an IPO, revealing financials and warning that its Claude models could exhibit harmful behaviors such as blackmail or resistance to shutdown.

items.title: Microsoft releases emergency .NET patches for critical Brotli flaw
items.summary: Microsoft issued emergency .NET updates to fix the Brotli vulnerability known as Broccoli2Shell, also tracked as HTTP2Shell.

items.title: Gheist Attackers Stumble in Attempt to Abuse GitHub Tokens
items.summary: A large‑scale GitHub campaign used stolen access tokens to target over 13,500 repositories with secret‑stealing workflows, but attackers faced obstacles.

items.title: Industrial Vendors Check Products for PHP2Shell Vulnerabilities
items.summary: Siemens, Schneider Electric, ABB and other industrial vendors confirmed that some of their products are affected by PHP2Shell vulnerabilities.

items.title: Genesys Hack Exposes Customer Data From Internal Systems
items.summary: A hack of Genesys internal systems exposed customer data; the Genesys Cloud and Engage platforms were not affected.

items.title: Stolen AI Reasoning Could Help China Build Cheaper Rivals
items.summary: Researchers discovered a flaw in OpenAI’s compaction process that allows transfer of reasoning traces between models, potentially enabling cheaper AI distillation for competitors.

items.title: Ukraine warns hackers are exploiting Chinese-made Dahua surveillance cameras
items.summary: Ukraine's CERT-UA reports that hackers have compromised Dahua internet‑connected cameras and video recorders, altering settings and creating unauthorized accounts.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: This2Shell, That2Shell, Everything's an RCE? Rogue AI, Supply Chain Chaos and More
items.summary: The week saw widespread remote code execution vulnerabilities, with attackers scanning and exploiting them. A leaked key exposed a software supply‑chain compromise.

items.title: When an AI Agent Is the Incident, the Identity Record Is the Evidence
items.summary: A new NIST, CISA, and NSA guide treats runaway AI agents as incidents to rehearse. The guide emphasizes establishing the agent’s authority before the incident occurs.

items.title: 10 Software Security Practices Built for the Next 250 Years
items.summary: The Cybersecurity Awareness Month theme "Securing the Next 250" encourages looking beyond vulnerabilities to build long‑term resilience. It outlines ten practices designed to safeguard digital systems for generations.

items.title: Linux Flaws Exposed Before Fixes as Root Exploit Goes Public
items.summary: Six Linux kernel flaws were publicly disclosed before fixes were merged, including one with a working root exploit. The exposure highlights a gap between vulnerability discovery and patch deployment.

items.title: Chinese man extradited for role in $36 million cryptocurrency scam
items.summary: A Chinese national was extradited from the Netherlands to the United States and arraigned in California for a cryptocurrency investment scam that stole nearly $37 million from 174 victims. The case underscores cross‑border cooperation in cyber‑crime investigations.

items.title: CISA publishes strategy with eye on the next four years
items.summary: CISA released a strategy review assessing its capabilities to meet the pillars of defend, harden, and prevail over the next four years. The document outlines plans to strengthen national cybersecurity posture.

items.title: PHP2Shell Exploitation Moves From Probes to Working Shells
items.summary: Attackers exploited PHP2Shell vulnerabilities against honeypots, launching 35 shells from two IP addresses on October 24. The incident demonstrates the transition from probing to active exploitation.

items.title: PHP2Shell: What to know about two critical PHP flaws
items.summary: CVE‑2026‑109618 and CVE‑2026‑109619 are critical PHP vulnerabilities. Website owners should patch promptly. Guidance is provided in a concise overview.

items.title: Kali Linux 2026.3 ships kernel 7.1.5, brings wardriving to the TicWatch Pro 3
items.summary: Kali Linux 2026.3 released with kernel 7.1.5 and updated build scripts, enabling containerized builds. The update also adds wardriving support for the TicWatch Pro 3.

items.title: Security pros reckon the biggest AI risk comes with an employee badge
items.summary: Security professionals cite employee misuse of AI tools, such as pasting company data, as the greatest risk. AI‑generated phishing was only a concern for a quarter of surveyed experts.

items.title: We shouldn't be surprised about the PHPocalypse, as the internet is built on sticks and glue
items.summary: Article warns that 75% of the web could be vulnerable to PHP flaws. Highlights the need for security awareness during Cybersecurity Awareness Month.

items.title: Microsoft Issues Emergency Patch Update for Critical .NET Buffer Overflow Flaw
items.summary: Microsoft released emergency patches for two new .NET buffer‑overflow vulnerabilities and unresolved issues from a prior release. Updates address critical security gaps.

items.title: UK Biobank back online soon, months after someone tried to sell 500k people's data on Alibaba
items.summary: UK Biobank will return online after security upgrades following an attempt to sell 500,000 individuals’ data on Alibaba. Awaiting UK government approval.

items.title: Two Critical Wasmtime Flaws Could Let Malicious WebAssembly Modules Escape Sandboxes
items.summary: Two critical Wasmtime vulnerabilities allow malicious WebAssembly modules to escape their sandbox on vulnerable builds. One flaw affects only ARM64. Fixed versions released.

items.title: PHP2Shell: No login, no app code, no warning. What next?
items.summary: Follow‑up on PHP2Shell explains exploitation details, current impact, and recommends rapid coverage using Tanium. Highlights zero‑auth attack vector.
